de.abas.eks.jfop.remote

Class FOe

  • Object
    • EKSe
      • FOe

  • public class FOe
extends EKSe
    This class provides FO accesses, whereby the individual methods have command-specific parameter lists respectively. In contrast to this, all methods of the class EKSe, from which this class inherits, have a standard string parameter.

      • input

        public static int input(String fopName,
                        boolean endCalledException)
                 throws FOPException
        Executes an embedded FOP. The specified program is executed within the Java program as an FO program. When it is ended, the control is given back to the Java program.
        Parameters:
        fopName - the FO program to be executed
        endCalledException - if true, an EndCalledException is generated if the FOP called ".end". You must note that in EFOPs however ".end" and ".end 0" mean there were no errors when ending. Furthermore, you must note that in command FOPs ".end" and ".continue" can be exchanged as required on the top level and that possibly ".end ." is used because of the closing of the output window without an error or cancelation situation existing.
        If false, no Exception is generated, if ".end" runs through. Please note that then ".end", ".end 0" and ".continue" output the exit status 0. This call is equivalent to FO.eingabe(String).
        Returns:
        exit status of the executed FO program according to the FO definition, i.e. ".end" and ".continue" and EOF mean exit status 0
        Throws:
        FOPException - if the embedded FOP cancels or is not executable
        EndCalledException - if the embedded FOP or called subprogram call ".end" and endCalledException==true applies.
